Of time, (a) c. gen. pers. in the time of: ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου; ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου; ἐπὶ Ἀβιάθαρ ἀρχιερέως, when A. was high priest (b) c. gen. rei, at, at the time of; ἐπὶ τ. προσευχῶν. II. C. dat. of place, answering the question, where? (a) lit. on, upon: al. after verbs of motion (v. supr. I, 1, (a)); above; at, by, al. (b) metaph. upon, on the ground of, (LXX); in the matter of; upon, of, concerning; of the ground, reason or motive, al. ἐφ’ ᾧ, for the reason that, because; after verbs of motion, over, al. of a condition (cl.); ἐπὶ δυσὶ μάρτυσιν; of purpose or aim; of authority, over; of hostility, c. dat. pers. (cl.), against; in addition to (cl.); of an adjunct, in, at, on. III. C. acc. 1. of place of motion upon or over, answering the question, whither? (a) lit. upon, over: al. mult. in NT also, answering the question, where? (as c. gen. dat.); ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, al. of motion to a vicinity, to, al. (b) metaph. (in wh. "the acc. is more widely prevalent than it strictly should be," Bl. §43, 1); of blessings, evils, etc. coming upon one, c. acc. pers. al. of addition (dat. in cl.), λύπη ἐπὶ λύπην; ἐπικαλεῖν ὄνομα ἐπί; καλεῖν ἐπί, to call after; of number or degree: ἐπὶ τρίς (cl. εἰς τ.), thrice; ἐπὶ πλεῖον, the more, further, (v. also infr. 2, (a)); ἐφ’ ὅσον, forasmuch as; of power, authority, control, al. of the direction of thoughts and feelings, unto, towards, al. of purpose, for; ἐφ’ ὅ πάρει (Rec. ἐφ’ ᾧ; of hostility, against; Of reference, concerning, for (cl. usually dat.). 2. Of time, (a) during, for: (WH, txt. omits ἐπί), al. ἐφ’ ὅσον (χρόνον), as long as, for so long time as, al. (for ἐφ’ ὅ in another sense, v. supr. 1, (b)); ἐφ’ ἱκανόν; ἐπὶ πλεῖον (v. supr. 1, (b)), yet longer, further (b) on, about, towards (cl. εἰς). IV. In composition, ἐπί signifies: up, ἐπαίρω; upon, ἐπίγειος, ἐπιδημέω, ἐπικαθίζω; towards, επιβλέπω, ἐπεκτείνω; over (of superintendence), ἐπιστάτης; again, in addition, ἐπαιτέω; against, ἐπιορκέω, ἐπιβουλή.

G1967.abbott_html: found only in the phrase ἄρτος ἐ. EV, daily; R, mg. for the coming day. (Several derivations find support, each pointing to a different meaning. 1. < ἐπιοῦσα (or, < ἐπὶ τὴν ἰοῦσαν, Zorell, s.v.), hence, for the morrow or for the coming day (R, mg.). 2. (a) < ἐπί + οὐσία, hence, for subsistence, needful (Am. R, mg.) (b) < ἐπί + εἶναι in fem. ptcp. form, hence, pertaining to (the day). For renderings of versions and views of various writers, v. reff. in DB, ext., 36 f. DCG, ii, 58 f. 62a; ICC on Lk, l.c. The EV, daily, is based on the Vg. (Lk; OL, Mt, Lk, quotidianus). "It is difficult not to think that τὸν ἐ. rests upon misunderstanding of an original Aramaic phrase, or upon a Greek corruption" (ICC on Mt, l.c. cf. also Cremer, 239).
